recipes.name: Kale Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 bunch kale, stems removed and leaves chopped
2 (15 ounce) cans cannellini beans (drained if desired)

steps.text: Heat olive oil in a large soup pot over medium-high heat; cook onion and garlic until soft, 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in kale and cook until wilted, about 2 minutes.
Stir in water, potatoes, beans, tomatoes, vegetable bouillon, parsley, and Italian seasoning.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until potatoes are cooked through, about 25 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Kale Soup
raw_recipe.description: This kale soup is a hearty and comforting vegetarian meal loaded with fresh kale, veggies, and creamy white beans in a deliciously savory broth.

video.description: If you wanted to try kale but didn’t know where to start, this is the video for you. Learn how to make a vegetarian soup where kale is the main ingredient. The soup is mild in flavor, yet filling and will certainly warm you up on a chilly night.

review.reviewBody: Easy, cheap and massive! I made this last night and had to transfer from a large pot to my largest soup pot, by the time I added the cannelini beans. Lesson 1, use a huge pot! My husband is NOT a kale fan, but he loved this and even packed a large bowl for his lunch today. Changes I made: 1. I don't use MSG, so instead of Knorr bouillon + water, I used 8 c. of veggie broth (can use homemade or a good, cheap version like Trader Joe's). I generously added Trocomare (organic leek/celery) salt as well as sea salt to help with flavor. 2. I didn't peel the potatoes before cubing and they were delicious. Changes I'll make next time: 1. Add a bay leaf; 2. Half the dried parsley from 2 Tbsp down to 1 Tbsp. A wonderful soup recipe and an easy way to eat the superfood kale!

This was a very good soup. I followed recipe except I added 3 garlic and herb chicken sausage links I crumbled them up and cooked in the large pot until they were browned and used only 1 tablespoon of olive oil, which I added while the sausage was cooking. Once the sausage browned I added ingredients as directed in this recipe. It is a very hardy soup with lots of flavor. I also replaced bullion with 32 ounces of prepared vegetable broth and added only 4 cups of water.

This soup is just fabulous. I made a double batch for church and did not bring any of it home! One gentleman ate three bowls and another gentleman asked for the recipe. I did use vegetable broth rather than the water and bouillon. I also also first cooked everything but the potatoes and beans for 45 minutes and then added them and cooked for another 45 minutes. It is just so yummy!!

Only made 2 changes. Instead of bouillon cubes I used vegetable Better Than Bouillon, and I added some Beyond Meat hot Italian sausage that I broke into pieces and sautéed first. Will definitely be making many more times to come. I think the Beyond sausage put it on another level Delicious

Made this in my instant pot came out delicious followed the instructions. I used sweet potato instead of potatoes and I seasoned my onions and garlic before I put my kale in . I don't measure so I can't tell you how much, also my beans were precooked and frozen in the freezer for dishes like this. I did add some onion powder and garlic powder and a sprinkle of Lawry's 15 min on high 10 min npr than quick release

I give it 3 stars because this is a good soup base recipe, but it needs A LOT of love before it is served. The broth will taste bland and resemble dirty bath water. Here are a few tips: -blend one can of the beans to use has a thickener -diced fire roasted tomatoes for more flavor -more garlic -If you want to keep it vegetarian use Premium Better Bouillon is seasoned but chicken broth has more flavor. -sautéed your greens very well with the onion and garlic. -with the soup is cook add garlic, onion, coriander powder. ENJOY! -add a bay

Very good. I made a few changes based on what I had on hand. I used one large sweet potato instead of the white potatoes and it was excellent ( I halved the recipe). It gave it a slightly sweet taste which we loved. I also added chopped carrots, green beans and frozen peas. It seems like a flexible recipe. Put in what you have on hand. I added a teaspoon of pesto at the end too. Very yummy. Thank you!

I like stews much more than soups, so I added barley (with the veg, but cook 45 minutes per the barley instructions) and left out most of the potatoes. Also, added a sliced carrot when I added all the veg. It was a huge hit at work today, so thank you!

Used this recipe as a starting point. Used spinach in lieu of kale, added broccoli, cauliflower and sweet potatoes; used thyme, Italian seasonings and bay leaf. Added a squeeze of lemon at the end with salt and pepper. Turned out great!

I substituted 1 can of Cannellini beans with kidney beans (only one at the store), 3/4ths of a bag of triple washed kale vs. what was called for, and I added 3 chicken bullion cubes in the recipe.

Simmered everthing in a dutch oven. Loved it and I will definitely make this again.

A very savory, flavorful and surprisingly hearty soup that was quick and easy to make.

While looking for a recipe including fresh kale I stumbled upon this and made it. Easy and excellent! A few notes: 1 - I did substitute low-sodium vegetable broth for the water and boullion cubes in an attempt to reduce sodium. Worked very well. 2 - As suggested by another reviewer, I substituted some of the potatoes for carrots; flavorful touch 3 - My hubby does not like kale, so I made this recipe in halves in two separate pots. In his, I did substitute fresh spinach; he loved the soup. Not a substitution, but an add-on. Just because I had a bit leftover in the fridge, I cubed some spiral-sliced ham in the soup to use it up. Yes, I did alter a bit, but I have no doubt that prepared "as written" would be just as tasty and satisfying. A bit of warm bread and a glass of wine -- an easy, filling, and delightful supper!

Easy to make and tastes great. Can substitute various ingredients for other things (cabbage for kale, sweet potato for potato, and chickpeas for butter beans, etc.,) - a good all-rounder! You can also add some dried chilli flakes if you want to spice it up a bit and serve up greater warmth in the winter months.
just tried this for a family get together -- I usually make a couple of chili options and veg beef soup....added this for the vegetarians of the family. They loved it and asked for the recipe! :).
This soup is soooo good my boyfriend and I love it.
Very good. I used both chicken and vegetable broth with only 2 cups water and also added crushed red pepper and some parmesan cheese.

We really loved this recipe. I've not eaten much kale, but it made this soup special due to its texture. I used the beans in my pantry, garbanzo and pinto. I think any bean will work fine. I only added some red pepper flakes to the pot and hot sauce in my bowls!
Used navy beans soaked overnight, and added 1 cup cubed kielbasa. It was great!

I enjoyed this easy, kind of rustic soup. Kale is not my favorite green, but I had some from my co op that I needed to use, and I liked it in this. Could also be good with sweet potatoes instead of white. I agree with adding the beans at the end (I also did not drain them). I added some red pepper flakes for a little extra flavor. I did not have vegetable bouillon cubes, so just used vegetable broth and chicken bone broth that I had on hand. It was even better the next day.
Delicious 😋!!!! We couldn't find the beans in the soup after it was cooked. So, I'll add them after the soup is cooked.

Soup was excellent! It's also very forgiving.. I subbed some kohlrabi and sweet potato in place of the white potato, and a can of garbanzo for 1 of the cans of white beans cuz that's what I had on hand. I also didn't drain/rinse the beans. Bit of paprika and cayenne as well.. it was terrific!!
